post.caption: Gold coins once sparked a germ scare. In 1908, the Mint began striking new gold coins with sunken designs. A Boston doctor proposed the style, and sculptor Bela Pratt designed them. The front showed a Native American in a feathered war bonnet. Sunken designs were meant to stack evenly and wear less. A Philadelphia coin dealer said the dents would hold dirt and germs. He called them the most unhygienic coins ever issued. The coins circulated anyway, and the smaller one became a Christmas gift. They are the only United States circulating coins with recessed designs. They were struck from 1908 to 1929.
